traps.shape: pattern A: the report states one general property over stored expressions; the same flaw exists at field select/update permissions, output/reduce field projection, function permissions and param permissions, so a solver that fixes only the first site it finds still fails
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; reason to dismiss: the report is about a table's PERMISSIONS, while field, function and param permissions are separate schema features

traps.shape: pattern A far module: a defined HTTP API endpoint's permission predicate runs on invocation
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; reason to dismiss: API handler bodies are supposed to write, so the API module looks intentionally permission-free

traps.shape: pattern B: event WHEN conditions and materialized/aggregated view conditions are definer-authored predicates evaluated with permission enforcement disabled; the same Options object also runs the trigger action / view maintenance, which must keep writing
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; reason to dismiss: these are triggers and views rather than PERMISSIONS clauses, and the condition shares Options with the action that legitimately writes

traps.shape: pattern B: ALTER stores a permission clause without the definition-time write check that DEFINE gained
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; reason to dismiss: ALTER is a modification, not a DEFINE, and the runtime guard already blocks the eventual write

traps.shape: input shape: a definition-time check that only inspects the top-level expression misses writes nested in IF/FOR blocks, LET/RETURN blocks and call arguments
traps.realistic_because: the published fix's own recursive walk shows the shape; reason to dismiss: a top-level statement check looks sufficient and nested blocks are assumed to be handled at runtime

traps.shape: injected sibling: ASSERT and VALUE expressions evaluated with permission enforcement disabled, so a write inside them bypasses the record user's permissions
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a maintainer treating schema validation/derived values as schema logic and disabling permission checks there; reachable through ordinary record CREATE/UPDATE; no deceptive names or comments
